title: Contextual kernel telemetry and span stitching for prefill/decode boundaries
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Current NVTX and tracing signals fragment kernel execution attribution across prefill and decode phases. When the scheduler splits a request across multiple kernel families (quantized vs full-precision, attention-fastpath vs fallback), existing spans either overlap, leave gaps, or produce high-cardinality noise that prevents accurate aggregation by model version, seq_len, and kernel variant. That obscures root cause for regressions and makes cost/latency trade-offs hard to quantify.

Goal: Implement a contextual telemetry layer that stitches NVTX ranges into coherent trace spans: (1) add lightweight scheduling boundary markers (sched_epoch_id) and kernel fingerprints to NVTX payloads; (2) coalesce adjacent NVTX ranges that belong to the same logical execution (prefill or decode) and emit single reconciled spans to the tracing exporter; (3) enrich per-kernel metrics with controlled tag set (model_version, quant_profile, seq_len_bucket, batch_size, kernel_family) while keeping cardinality bounded.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end traces show a single prefill span and decode span per request with correct duration summing to observed token latency (within sampling error).
- Per-kernel metrics attribute >=95% of GPU time to a kernel_family + quant_profile bucket in the nightly perf rollup.
- Dashboards can slice token latency regressions by kernel_family and seq_len_bucket without exploding metrics cardinality.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) NVTX payload schema: encode a 64-bit envelope with flags + sched_epoch_id + kernel_sig_hash. Keep format extensible and versioned.
2) Runtime hooks: when scheduler schedules work, emit boundary NVTX markers with sched_epoch_id and phase (PREFILL/DECODE). On kernel entry/exit, emit NVTX with kernel_sig_hash and small tag id (quant/profile id). Avoid full string tags in hotpath.
3) Kernel fingerprinting: compute a stable 16-bit kernel_family id at model load time from (op_signature, quant_level, kernel_impl_id). Use this id in NVTX to reduce span-tag cardinality.
4) Exporter changes: update the tracing exporter to stitch NVTX ranges by sched_epoch_id and phase, collapse contiguous ranges from the same kernel_family into a single span with aggregated counters (gpu_cycles, avg_exec_ms, call_count).
5) Sampling and aggregation: implement adaptive sampling on high QPS paths to preserve correlation between spans and metrics; export full-resolution traces for a small percentage of requests and aggregated metrics for all.
6) Telemetry backend: add derived metrics and pre-rolled aggregation queries (by kernel_family, seq_len_bucket) and dashboard tiles.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- NVTX overhead: adding payloads increases driver work; to mitigate, use compact binary envelope and emit only on kernel boundaries + scheduling markers, not per-sub-kernel micro-ops.
- Cardinality: avoid freeform strings; emit small numeric ids and maintain server-side mapping tables for lookups in dashboards/PRs.
- Accuracy vs overhead: full-resolution tracing is expensive; use sampling + aggregated counters to keep cost predictable.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for kernel_sig_hash determinism and envelope decode.
- Integration test harness: synthetic workloads to validate that stitched spans equal observed per-request latency across sequence-length distribution (1..2048).
- Perf regression bench: compare base runtime with telemetry on at scale and verify <2% tail-latency overhead at P95 for sampled traces.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag telemetry on by default in staging and opt-in in production.
- Canary on 5% of requests in production for 48h with close monitoring of GPU driver errors and latency.
- Gradually increase to 25% then 100% after 7 days of stable signals.

Dashboards and alerts:
- New dashboard: kernel-family latency heatmap (x: seq_len_bucket, y: kernel_family) with tokens/sec and p95 latency.
- Alert: sudden >15% increase in unattributed GPU time or growth in 'unknown_kernel' bucket.

Open questions / blockers:
- Do we want the kernel_family mapping to be stable across deploys or per-runtime-instance? (Prefer stable across deploys for aggregated dashboards, but requires careful emitting of mapping diffs.)
- How to surface kernel mapping to customers in a privacy-safe way? (Consider redaction or only exposing public-friendly labels.)

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Telemetry+Envelope+Design
- Exporter PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892
- Dashboard draft (Looker/Observability): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/rt-kernel-telemetry
comments: 2026-02-13: Initial write-up and RFC posted to runtime channel. Feedback from Marcus: prefer 32-bit compact payload rather than 64-bit to reduce ioctl overhead — decided to keep 64-bit for future extension.

2026-02-19: Spike complete. Measured NVTX emit cost (~120ns per envelope) using synthetic workload; overhead acceptable when sampled. Added kernel_sig_hash prototype in branch feature/telemetry-fingerprint. (PR: /runtime/compare/telemetry-spike)

2026-02-26: Design review with infra/observability. Decided to store human-readable mapping in a separate low-cardinality table and only emit numeric ids in hotpath. Action: Elena to create mapping API and migration plan.

2026-03-05: Implemented exporter stitcher and unit tests. Local integration test shows prefill+decode spans stitch correctly for 99% of requests in sample workload. Edge case: interleaved kernels from background eviction threads can create overlapping ranges — added thread_owner_id to NVTX envelope to disambiguate.

2026-03-12: Canary started at 5% of prod traffic. Initial telemetry dashboards look correct; small uptick in driver warnings investigated and traced to a mismatched NVTX version on one AMI — ops rolling AMI patch.
2026-03-13: Removed experimental debug tags from hotpath; preparing release notes for runtime-1.22.
